title: Webb County Approves Reinvestment Zones for Six Renewable Energy Projects
excerpt: Webb County Commissioners approved creating reinvestment zones for six renewable energy projects on Friday, the first step toward possible tax breaks. No tax breaks were approved at the meeting.
content:
The Webb County Commissioners Court approved creating reinvestment zones for six renewable energy projects at its meeting Friday, November 13, according to KGNS.

The zones are the first step toward possible tax breaks for the projects, KGNS reported. No tax breaks were approved at the meeting.

The six projects named are Solar C, Solar D, Solar E, Solar F, Solar G and the El Corazon project, described as solar or wind projects, according to KGNS. No companies behind the projects were named in the report.

The reinvestment zones remain active for five years, during which the county and each project's owners can agree on possible tax breaks, KGNS reported.

Commissioner Rosaura "Wawi" Tijerina said, "We've seen that wind is something that can be very beneficial to the county, and we have some experience with that." County Judge Tano Tijerina said the zones "are also good to have ... because they can also bring some sort of a development agreement," and said the projects will bring jobs, investment and tax revenue to the county, according to KGNS.

The move comes as Webb County is seeing increased interest in renewable energy development, KGNS reported. Commissioners previously approved similar zones for three solar projects, Pinto and Mesquite 1 and 2.

Webb Watch 956 previously reported that commissioners were set to consider three renewable energy zones at their November 9 meeting. The November 13 vote covers six projects.

Source: KGNS, November 13, 2026.
